It’s not all logos and sunshine.

Okay, sometimes it is. Especially here in San Diego. But there’s a lot more that goes into building a brand people actually trust and love. A lot more.

Good brands don’t happen by accident. They’re built on alignment.

Today marks three years without a drink.

This wasn’t even something I planned to post about this year, which feels very different from the first two. I’ve been trying to understand why it doesn’t feel any easier than before, and the only thing that keeps coming to mind is this: maybe it’s because the world hasn’t gotten any easier either?

After year 1, I felt like I could conquer just about anything. Sharing it felt fulfilling too. There was a wave of support, and messages from people saying it helped them on their own path, which in turn helped me. Year two felt similar, just a bit quieter. And that was okay.

This past year has brought some of the biggest challenges I’ve ever faced. I’m proud of myself for moving through them like I have, even though I’m still working through a lot. In that context, celebrating not drinking almost feels laughable. Although maybe the celebration isn’t the number or a streak at all. Maybe it’s that I didn’t give in even when there was no light to see or air to breathe.

Ultimately, this year I learned how to fall better.

Skateboarding taught me that falling can be beautiful. You eat it on the ruthless concrete. Hard. But if you stick with it long enough, you learn how to fall well. You tuck. You roll. You protect. You get back up a little faster each time. The falls don’t hurt less, but you do trust yourself more.

This year was filled with many soul crushing falls, but I’m also deeply aware that so many people are carrying far, far more than I can ever imagine. My heart is entirely with them. And I suppose that’s why posting about my own 3 year streak of sobriety doesn’t feel as easy as the first 2.

But I want to use it as a moment to say this:
No matter how hard it gets, you are incredible.
You’re incredible if you resist the crutch and fight through it. And you’re incredible if you fall, get up the next day, and try again. That’s what this beautiful life that we were gifted is all about, isn’t it?

Picking ourselves back up.
Learning how to fall.
And giving it a better shot.
Over and over again.

Love,
Johnny

Ahh… to design a personal brand that feels ethereal, like a sunset washing over a Caribbean beach in Mexico. To play with the idea of thread unraveling from Greek mythology. To build something flexible enough to hold all sides of her. The mystic. The guide. The seeker. The lover. All moving within a divine feminine playfulness.

Designing a brand like this for Ariadna, or for any of my clients, never comes from my own ego or from wanting to make something that looks a certain way. That’s not why I started my creative studio. 

It comes from deep strategy sessions where we uncover, together, what they are ready to shed and what they are becoming. And along the way, I discover so much about myself too. Gold dripping down tropical flowers? Never an idea I would have arrived at on my own. 

It felt more like once we got to the foundation of the personal brand and where she’s headed, that a creative force flowed through me that wasn’t my own. It was for her. As Rick Rubin often reminds us, the best creative work does not come from forcing ideas, but from allowing them to move through you once you get out of the way.

#personalbrand #brandstrategist #personalbrandingagency

Why ditch a career you love?

And what do you do when your entire identity is built around it?

For me, it began when I started paying attention to my intuition after 30 or so years. It arrives as a quiet whisper that sometimes feels impossible to hear, especially when the louder voice is the one that wants you to stay where you are (safe). That louder one was my ego.

In 2020 I pivoted from architecture into digital design. I went from designing spaces most architects dream of to building brands and websites. My bigger clients were Spotify and Disney. And after almost two years of my ego being overly stoked, I left again. I listened to the humble whisper that there was more. That I AM more.

I’m not alone in seeking the full potential of life. Harrison Ford was a carpenter before Hollywood. Julia Child wrote her first cookbook at fifty. My mom left ultrasonography in her sixties, after raising five kids, to pursue holistic nutrition. She’s a dope mom. 

Most people reach a point where the thing they built no longer energizes them. You wake up and realize you’ve outgrown the version of yourself who made all these earlier choices. And it takes more courage to follow the whisper than to keep doing the thing you already know how to do.

You are allowed to choose again. And again. And again. Keep following your beautiful gut. 

The artwork in this post is titled Whispering Intuition by yours truly, Johnny Lemoine.

#intuition #spiritualgrowth #kinetictypography #mindfulness #careerchange #careercoaching

Ever been told you’re too much? Too loud, too wild, too weird? Too old to be doing something? I sure have. And for a while, I believed it. But the older I get, the clearer that all becomes bullshit. Society might try to shrink you, but the universe has other plans. Our soul knows better. The universe rewards expansion. 

Enaytime came from that expansion. Camp Kölsch is just one flavor, but it’s a whole world of weird. An astronaut strumming guitar by the fire. One backpacking through a portal. Another floating downstream in a crescent moon-kayak. I drew them with the same wonder I had as a kid. And released Enaytime as a celebration of being a few years sober (a big moment of expansion).

This design is for the ones who feel everything. Who live fully. Who don’t water themselves down to make others comfortable. So I’m curious, what’s your favorite part of the illustration? And how do you stay wild in a world that wants you tame?

Dance into the Revolution.

I happily poured my heart into Revolution’s brand strategy—defining the value proposition, connecting with the target audience, analyzing competitors, and refining the brand voice and messaging. This project wasn’t just about creating something visually appealing—it was about architecting a brand that embodies authenticity, disrupts the norm, and stands the test of time. As someone deeply passionate about house music, dancing, and festivals, bringing this vision to life was incredibly meaningful. And after nearly two years of sobriety, designing a non-alcoholic event in San Diego, especially as the first of its kind, was a project that felt personal and important.

The design captures that same energy. The primary logo steps into a new dimension of sound, with the “R” leg jutting out—pushing boundaries and embracing underground culture. These elements are carried through across each visual touchpoint, from event posters to social media, ensuring the brand is alive, energetic, and true to its roots.

This work is more than just a project; it’s a reflection of a culture that I live for—authentic, bold, and deeply tied to the music and the people who make it special.

If you’re thinking of creating a brand that resonates and makes an impact, let’s connect. Let’s build something unforgettable together.

@djmagofficial @housemusic.us @insomniacevents #edm #housemusic #housemusicfamily #genefarris #revolutionedm #undergroundhouse #brandagency #freelancegraphicdesigner

Taking on this project I knew I wasn’t designing a brand—I was building a foundation for a movement in music. I built a full in-depth brand strategy that not only defines the essence of what Revolution stands for, but also gives the brand a structure strong enough to grow, evolve, and connect with its audience. With Lemoine, it is never about following trends. It’s about creating something real, something that transcends the typical and becomes a cultural movement. That is Revolution. 

The brand strategy guided every decision: from the bold visual identity to the tone and voice that would speak directly to the community. If you work with us, you’ll know immediately that we don’t just create a cool logo or some flashy graphics—but we ensure the brand’s message is authentic, the experience is immersive, and every part of the design is connected to the core values. For Revolution, that’s authenticity, community, and creativity.

With this strategic foundation in place first, I then design the visual identity to bring it to life. From typography to textures to motion, every element was intentionally crafted to reflect the underground roots of house music while making it modern and accessible. Revolution isn’t just a San Diego-based event—it’s a global movement that connects people through the power of music and community.

This project is a true reflection of how design and strategy can work hand-in-hand to create something that’s not just aesthetically pleasing, but impactful and long-lasting. It’s a proud moment to see the strategy I laid out come to life in such a real and meaningful way. Revolution is just getting started, and I’m excited to see where it goes.

Two years sober today. Let’s. Fucking. Go. It feels like a lifetime and a blink all at once. This milestone represents more than just time; it’s a testament to the power of choosing integrity, health, and self-love over everything else, every single damn day. Living this way has brought me clarity, strength, and blessings I never thought possible—dreams coming to life, deeper connections, and creativity that feels completely off the charts.

Every day, I honor the rituals that have guided me here: meditation, yoga, yoga nidra, freezing ocean swims, breathwork, and treating each day as a ceremony itself (because it’s truly mind blowing we get to be here at all). With mindfulness at the core of it all, I’m growing—sometimes with grace, sometimes with stumbles, but always forward. Life isn’t always easy, but it feels like I’m becoming more of the person I’m meant to be, piece by piece, heelflip to heelflip.

What I’ve learned is that vulnerability creates connection. Since sharing my journey, so many have reached out for support, and that means the world to me. No matter what negativity or demons cross my path, I’ll always show up with love—for myself and for those around me.

Thank you for being part of this journey. Here’s to living with intention, honoring the process, and celebrating every moment of growth.

Love you very much. Truly. 

—Johnny

Bariq represents so much more than wine—it’s about honoring the strength of the past while celebrating the abundance and light of today.

I’m thrilled to share Bariq, a project that is deeply connected to culture, history, and personal growth. As I design the branding and packaging for this Armenian winery, I’m just a few days away from celebrating two years sober. Being able to work on something tied to alcohol as a proud sober man feels empowering—a reminder of how far I’ve come and how meaningful this journey is.

Bariq is connected to the soul of Armenia. The vineyard is surrounded by ancient churches, kachkars (intricate stone crosses), and petroglyphs etched into the earth, each telling a story of resilience and interconnectedness. These aren’t just symbols—they’re a living connection to history, to the people who carved them, and to the Armenian land itself.

The Bariq logotype reflects this perfectly. Its bold forms embody strength and resilience, while the elegant curves and intricate details bring a sense of playfulness and light. It’s a celebration of harvest, abundance, and the beauty of honoring where we come from while embracing where we’re headed.

Bariq isn’t just a brand—it’s a story. It’s a tribute to the strength of ancestors, the cycles of renewal in the vines, and the light we create and share. Working on this has reminded me that every harvest, whether of wine, growth, or creativity, carries its own abundance.

Here’s to strength, light, and the stories that connect us.
